description: Five sample calls with their real Deepgram transcripts, labelled by hand from each script. Agent is always speaker 0. Run `php artisan qa:eval`.

cases.description: US live transfer, fully compliant 20-year term sale (Sarah Mitchell)

segments.text: Hi, Robert. Thanks for holding while my colleague transferred you over.
This is Sarah Mitchell, a licensed life insurance agent with Summit Life Agency.
Before we start, this call is recorded for quality and compliance purposes.
Is that okay with you?
Yeah. That's fine.
Great.
And just to confirm, you filled out a form online asking us to call you about life insurance. Is that right?
Yes. That was me.
I put my details in last night.
Perfect.
So I'm calling about your request for a life insurance quote, and I'd love to help you find the right fit.
Do you have about ten minutes?
Sure. Go ahead.
Thank you.
And which state are you in, Robert?
I want to make sure I'm licensed there.
Ohio.
Great. I'm licensed in Ohio.
To recommend the right policy, may I ask a few quick questions?
Could you tell me your age?
Thank you.
Do you currently have any life insurance through work or on your own?
Just the policy through my job.
I think it's one year of salary.
That's common, but it usually ends if you leave the job.
Do you have children or anyone else who relies on your income?
Yes. My wife and two kids.
They're eight and 11.
Thank you.
And do you have a mortgage?
Yes. About $200,000
left on it.
Okay.
Any health conditions I should know about, like diabetes,
heart problems, or any medications you take?
Just blood pressure medication.
It's well controlled.
That's helpful. Thank you.
And what monthly budget would you be comfortable with for this?
Maybe 40 or $50 a month.
That works well.
Based on what you've told me, I'd suggest a twenty year term life policy with $250,000
of coverage.
That would cover the mortgage and see both kids through school.
With your age and health, that would likely come in around 41 to $46
a month.
How does that sound?
That sounds reasonable.
Good.
I do want to be clear that the final price depends on the carriers underwriting,
and they may ask a few more health questions.
It's not guaranteed to be approved at that rate, but from what you've told me it should go smoothly.
Okay. Understood.
Also, once your policy is issued, you have a thirty day free look period.
If you change your mind for any reason, you can cancel for a full refund.
Good to know.
Who would you like to name as the beneficiary?
My wife, Linda.
Thank you.
So the next step is I'll send you an email with the quote and a secure link to complete the application.
The carrier will follow-up within two business days, and nothing is charged until the policy is approved.
Does that sound good?
Yes. Perfect.
Thanks, Sarah.
You're welcome, Robert.
Have a great evening.

expected.notes: Full name and agency: "This is Sarah Mitchell, a licensed life insurance agent with Summit Life Agency."
Recording notice given before any personal questions.
"I'm calling about your request for a life insurance quote."

expected.criterion_name: Needs Discovery – Age and Health Status
expected.notes: Asks age and health/medications before recommending.

expected.criterion_name: Needs Discovery – Existing Cover and Dependants
expected.notes: Asks about current cover (work policy) and family who rely on the income.
Asks for a monthly budget before quoting.

expected.criterion_name: Product Explanation – Coverage Amount and Term
expected.notes: $250,000 over a twenty-year term.
Says approval is not guaranteed.
No urgency or pressure.
Explains the 30-day free-look period with a full refund.
Email with quote and application link; carrier follows up in two business days.

cases.description: US live transfer, final expense: no recording notice, first name only, no discovery, no free-look, vague close (James O'Brien)

segments.text: Hey there. This is James with Summit Life Agency. You just got transferred over to me about the final expense coverage.
Oh, okay.
Yes.
Great. Can I get your full name and date of birth so I can pull up some rates?
Sure. It's Dorothy Miller, 03/10/1958.
Perfect. And your address?
42 Birchwood Avenue, Tampa, Florida.
Alright, Dorothy. I can get you a whole life final expense policy with $15,000
of coverage.
The premium would be $62
a month. How does that sound?
Is that the best you can do?
That's the standard rate for your age. It's a really good price.
Okay. I suppose I can think about it.
Great. Should I go ahead and get that set up for you? Maybe.
Can you send me the details first?
Sure thing. I'll mail those over. Thanks, Dorothy.

expected.notes: Gives only his first name ("this is James"); the criterion requires the full name.
No recording notice at all (critical).
"You just got transferred over to me about the final expense coverage."

expected.criterion_name: Needs Discovery – Age and Health Status
expected.notes: Takes the date of birth but never asks about health before quoting.

expected.criterion_name: Needs Discovery – Existing Cover and Dependants
expected.notes: Neither existing cover nor dependants discussed.
Premium quoted with no budget discussion.

expected.criterion_name: Product Explanation – Coverage Amount and Term
expected.notes: $15,000 of whole life final expense coverage.
No guarantee claims.
Asks once to set it up and accepts "send me the details first".
Free-look / cancellation period never mentioned.
"I'll mail those over" does not explain what happens next.

cases.description: UK call, good in every way except the missing recording notice (Priya Sharma)

segments.text: Good afternoon. This is Priya Sharma from INSURVAS Insurance.
Is this mister Davidson?
Yes. Speaking.
Great.
I'm calling because you submitted an inquiry about life insurance last week and I wanted to follow-up.
Is now a good time?
Yes. That's fine.
Brilliant.
To point you toward the right product, can I ask a few questions?
Firstly, how old are you? I'm 51.
And are you generally in good health?
Anything significant to mention?
I had a minor heart scare about four years ago, but I've been clear since and I'm on a low dose aspirin.
Thank you for sharing that.
Do you currently have any life insurance in place?
No. I had a policy but it expired last year and I didn't renew it.
And do you have a partner or children who depend on your income?
My wife and we have a son at university.
Understood.
What kind of monthly budget are you working with?
I'd say 50 to £80.
Based on your age and health history, a level term policy would probably work well.
over fifteen years, you might expect to pay around 60 to £75
a month, though that could be affected by the cardiac history. So underwriting will confirm the exact rate.
Okay.
I'd want to know the exact figure before committing.
Absolutely.
That's sensible.
You'd only commit once you've seen the confirmed premium.
Also, after the policy is issued, you'd have a thirty day cooling off period to change your mind and get a full refund.
Okay. Good to know.
So the next steps are, I'll email you a summary and illustration, and the underwriting team will follow-up within two working days with a full quote based on your health details.
That sounds fine.
Thank you, Priya.
Thank you for your time. Have a good afternoon.

expected.notes: Full name and company.
No recording notice (critical).
"I'm calling because you submitted an enquiry about life insurance."

expected.criterion_name: Needs Discovery – Age and Health Status
expected.notes: Age and health asked before recommending.

expected.criterion_name: Needs Discovery – Existing Cover and Dependants
expected.notes: Existing cover and dependants both asked.
Budget asked before quoting.

expected.criterion_name: Product Explanation – Coverage Amount and Term
expected.notes: £300,000 over fifteen years.
Says underwriting will confirm the rate.
Supports the customer waiting for the exact figure.
30-day cooling-off period with a full refund.
Email summary and underwriting follow-up within two working days.

cases.description: UK call with guaranteed-approval claims and almost no discovery (Daniel Hughes)

segments.text: Good morning. This is Daniel Hughes from INSURVAS Insurance.
This call may be recorded.
I'm calling about your life insurance inquiry.
Yes. I filled in a form online.
Great.
I've got some really exciting news for you. We have a product that offers guaranteed acceptance, no medical questions,
no health checks, everyone is approved.
You cannot be turned down.
Oh, that sounds interesting.
I have some health issues so I was worried about getting cover.
With this product you don't need to worry at all. Guaranteed approval regardless of your health history. You're in.
That does sound appealing.
Can I ask your age and roughly what level of cover you're thinking?
I'd like maybe a £100,000
to leave for my kids.
Perfect.
At 62 with guaranteed acceptance,
we can absolutely get that sorted for you. The premium would be around £85
a month.
Is there any cooling off period if I change my mind?
Yes. There's a standard thirty day cancellation window once the policy is issued.
Okay.
What happens next?
I'll get your application started now.
I just need a few details. Your full name, address, date of birth, and bank details for the direct debit.
I can give you my name and address but I'd rather not give bank details over the phone today.
That's completely
fine. I'll email you a secure link to complete the application online
including the payment setup.
The next step summary will come through today.
Alright. Thank you.
Thank you. I'll get that sent over now.

expected.notes: Full name and company.
"This call may be recorded" at the start.
"I'm calling about your life insurance enquiry."

expected.criterion_name: Needs Discovery – Age and Health Status
expected.notes: Asks age only; health never asked (and dismissed with "guaranteed acceptance").

expected.criterion_name: Needs Discovery – Existing Cover and Dependants
expected.notes: Agent never asks about existing cover or dependants.
Premium quoted with no budget discussion.

expected.criterion_name: Product Explanation – Coverage Amount and Term
expected.notes: Cover amount comes from the customer; no term is ever stated.
"Guaranteed acceptance… everyone is approved. You cannot be turned down." (critical)
Overselling, but no urgency; accepts the customer declining bank details.
Confirms the 30-day cancellation window (when asked) before any payment.
Emails a secure application link and a next-steps summary.

cases.description: UK call, complete discovery but subtle urgency about an "enhanced rate this week" (Emma Clarke)

segments.text: Hello. This is Emma Clark from INSURVAS Insurance.
This call may be recorded for quality purposes.
Is that okay?
Yes. Fine.
Great.
I'm calling because you inquired about life insurance recently.
I'm glad I caught you today because we have an enhanced rate available this week that I want to make sure you know about.
Oh, right.
What does that mean?
It means the underwriters are offering slightly lower premiums for new applications submitted this week. It's a pricing window they open periodically,
and it won't be available indefinitely.
So it's worth exploring while it's on the table.
I see.
How long does it last?
It typically closes by end of week, sometimes sooner depending on application volumes.
Let me get some details from you so we can take advantage of it. How old are you?
And are you in good health?
Yes. Generally healthy.
Do you have dependents, a partner, or kids?
Yes. Wife and two kids.
An existing cover.
A small employer policy.
Budget per month.
Maybe 40 to £60.
Perfect.
For your profile, I'd suggest 250,000
over twenty years, likely around 35 to £45
a month at the enhanced rate. If we can get your application in this week, you'd lock in the lower
price. The cooling off period is thirty days if you change your mind once it's issued.
I'm not sure I want to rush into this.
I completely understand.
I just want to make sure you have all the information so you can decide.
The enhanced rate really is worth acting on while it's there.
Okay. What do you need from me?
I'll email you the summary and application link today.
Please do try to complete it within the next few days to secure the rate. Shall I send that over now?
Yes. Okay. Go ahead.
Brilliant.
Thank you for your time.
I'll get that sent right away.

expected.notes: Full name and company.
Recording notice at the start.
"I'm calling because you enquired about life insurance recently."

expected.criterion_name: Needs Discovery – Age and Health Status
expected.notes: Age and health asked.

expected.criterion_name: Needs Discovery – Existing Cover and Dependants
expected.notes: Dependants and existing cover asked.
Budget asked before quoting.

expected.criterion_name: Product Explanation – Coverage Amount and Term
expected.notes: £250,000 over twenty years.
No guarantee claims.
"Won't be available indefinitely… closes by end of week… worth acting on" after the customer says they do not want to rush (critical).
